main.description: Revoke an identity's access: write the deny record FIRST, then delete the ServiceAccount and the name-keyed artifacts, and leave the grant record in a terminal Revoked state rather than deleting it. The order is the whole design - a revocation that only deletes objects is a ten-second interruption, because getKubeconfig is create-on-read and would re-arm the identity on the next call. The principal comes from the VERIFIED token's iss and never from this input. Answers 202: propagation is a controller's work plus the authenticator's own latency, so a synchronous response would be dishonest.

did.description: The identity to revoke. Absent or equal to the caller's own DID means self-revocation. Any other value is an operator revocation and requires the caller's DID to be on the operator allowlist.

name.description: The cluster label to revoke on. Absent means every cluster of the account, including clusters created after this call - the account-level deny is the fan-out root and is reachable while every cluster is COLD.

errors.name: InvalidRequest
errors.description: did is not a DID, or name is not a legal RFC-1123 label within 63 characters.

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.description: Missing or invalid service-auth token. Also returned when the token's aud is not this service or its lxm is not this method.

errors.name: Forbidden
errors.description: did names an identity other than the caller's, and the caller is not on the operator allowlist. Not retryable.

errors.name: ClusterNotFound
errors.description: name was given and this account has no cluster of that name.

name.description: The cluster label, or empty for an account-level revocation.

state.description: RevocationPending is the alarm, not a failure: the deny is already written and the identity is already refused, while the controller works through the deletions. Revoked is terminal and survives until its cluster does.
